Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has promised traders at the New Benin Market in Benin City that their complaints about excessive taxation will be settled soon. The governor made the pledge on Wednesday while addressing traders and market leaders during a rally the All Progressives Congress (APC) held at the market. The governor recalled that he visited the market during his campaign and promised to return if elected. He also said he had pledged to tar the access roads within and around the market. “I remember when I was contesting, I came and sat down here that very day. I told you that when you vote for me, I will come back. I am back now,” he said. He said traders had earlier complained of unstable electricity supply, and that he would direct the Edo State Electrification Agency (EDSEA) to find the cause of the problem. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “If it is a transformer, we will get you a new one. What we are after is to provide you with a good life. Your vote was for me to provide you with a good life,” he said. On taxation, the Chairman of the Mother Union in the market, Mr Taiwo Aideyan appealed to the governor to reduce the levies imposed on traders. Okpebholo responded that he would meet the market leadership on Thursday in his office, together with the Chairman of the Edo State Board of Internal Revenue. “We are going to resolve the issue of tax by Thursday in my office with your leaders and the state chairman of the Board of Internal Revenue, so that your leaders can tell us what you can pay. The tax issue will die completely, so that you can do your business very well,” he said. The governor also assured members of the Igbo community in Edo State that they would be fairly represented in his administration. He appealed to them to vote for President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates in the forthcoming general election. Earlier, Aideyan commended the governor for ending illegal ticketing in the market and for improving security across the state. Another market leader, Mr John Ogbu, praised Okpebholo’s developmental projects, saying his achievements in two years as governor were commendable. “This is the only governor in the history of the state who has appointed an Igbo man to his cabinet in the person of Comrade Martins Oli Anayor,” Ogbu said.
